subject: Intro + workload snapshot for onboarding — model shortlist & context needs

Subject: Intro + workload snapshot for onboarding — model shortlist & context needs

Hi Samir / Alicia — great to kick this off. I’m Logan, your CS lead for the NovaTex pilot. To get Ben and the implementation team the right model shortlist and sizing, can you send a quick workload snapshot? If easier, fill the attached CSV stub (I’ll attach a token/profile template in a follow-up).

Quick asks (bullet list is fine):
- Average prompt tokens and example prompt types (classification vs summarization vs conversational)
- Average response tokens and 95th percentile response tokens
- Peak concurrent QPS (or peak RPS) and typical hourly distribution (UTC)
- Conversation context length requirement (how many prior turns / tokens should be preserved)
- Latency SLO (p95 target) and any strict max latency for interactive flows
- Any PII/security flags (PHI, PCI, regulated fields) we should know for routing / private deployment

If you have sample prompts or a CSV export, please attach. We’ll produce a short model shortlist + sizing recommendation within 48 business hours after we see the numbers.

Thanks — Logan
Logan Wright | Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@novatex.io>

Date: 2027-11-02T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + workload snapshot for onboarding — model shortlist & context needs

Thanks Logan — attaching our abbreviated export (nova_workload_summary.csv) and a small sample set (example_prompts.txt). Answers inline below.

- Avg prompt tokens: ~120 tokens (many short form questions), sample prompts attached.
- Avg response tokens: ~60 tokens; 95th pct response tokens: ~850 tokens (long summarization of encounter notes).
- Peak concurrent QPS: ~450 qps (we see traffic spikes around 09:00-11:00 and 17:00-18:00 UTC).
- Conversation context need: for the triage flow we want to preserve ~6 prior turns (~4k tokens); for full clinical summaries we need up to 10k tokens (longest flows).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 700ms for triage UI; for batched summary jobs up to 5s is acceptable.
- Security: data includes limited PHI; we will require SOC2 and contractual controls, likely will need a Private or Dedicated deployment for prod.

Let me know if you need anything else. Samir
Samir Khan | Head of Integrations | NovaTex Health
Attachments: nova_workload_summary.csv (csv), example_prompts.txt (txt)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Intro + workload snapshot for onboarding — model shortlist & context needs

Thanks Samir — helpful data. I pulled a first-pass model shortlist and a sizing sketch — attaching a PDF with details (redwood_model_shortlist.pdf). Key notes below: 

Model shortlist (prioritized by latency × cost × context support):
1) redwood-3.5-std-16k — balanced: 16k context, good latency for interactive, cost-effective with quantization on our runtime.
2) llama-70b-8k-qa-quant — strong QA/LLM reasoning where context is <8k tokens; higher cost but better single-request accuracy on deep summaries.
3) gptj-6b-refined (open) — fallback for non-sensitive batch workloads; lower cost, lower latency, limited context.

Sizing and recommendations (baseline pilot):
- Baseline capacity for pilot (supporting 450 qps peak with p95 <=700ms): reserve 3 x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) with autoscale + burst to 4 during peak; this assumes batching window 20ms and our standard KV-cache for repeated context across a user session.
- For long-form summaries (10k context) route to a separate pool tuned for longer-seq execution to avoid impacting triage latency. One optimally-configured worker can handle ~60 concurrent long-summary streams with 1–2s per-token behavior — recommend 2 workers for headroom.
- Token budget estimate (very rough): avg tokens per request = prompt(120) + response(60) = 180 tokens; peak qps 450 → peak token/sec ≈ 81k tokens/sec → monthly token estimate for 30-day month (assuming 6 peak hours/day + baseline 25% off-peak) ≈ 3.2B tokens. We'll refine after seeing hourly distribution CSV.
- Caching: enable prefix cache for repeated system prompts and KV-cache for conversation state — expect ~20–35% token savings on triage flows.
- Quantization: for non-sensitive batch jobs, use 4-bit quantized variants to cut GPU footprint by ~2–3x. For PHI flows we recommend Dedicated (data in transit + at rest controls) and possibly Private later.

Next steps: I’ll work with Marissa on a brief mutual action plan and proposed pilot dates. If NovaTex prefers to reduce reserved capacity, we can propose a gradual ramp with metric gates (latency and error budgets).

— Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_model_shortlist.pdf (pdf)

Thanks Ben — couple quick clarifying Qs: 
1) For the triage flow, is 16k context necessary? It seems overkill if most prompts are 120 tokens; could we use an 8k model and fall back to long-pool for the small % of 10k summaries?
2) Can you estimate incremental monthly cost delta between the 3x A100 baseline and a 2x baseline with more aggressive batching? We're evaluating capex/opex trade-offs.
3) Cold-start behavior — when autoscale spins up extra workers during a spike, what latency hit should we expect for the first few requests?

Samir

Great alignment team — thank you all. Quick confirmations from Redwood side:
- Ben will post the benchmark results to the Drive folder by EOD 11/08.
- We’ll prototype the triage route on redwood-3.5-std-16k but can instrument an 8k variant and A/B the two for cost/latency in pilot.
- Cold-start: expect a 1–2s latency bump for the first request when a new worker spins up; we’ll include pre-warm rules for predicted peaks to minimize this.

I’ll send a calendar invite for the integration kickoff (11/10, 10:00 UTC). Looking forward to the pilot.
